summary: This costs one check and routes nothing, so its value depends on what it replaces. It is worth running because bf16-lossless-exp4-warpspec-persistent-stage3 is still queued at p1 even though LESSONS (2026-10-25) already calls the line dead. The probe is the cheapest way to settle that conflict for good. Two conditions: stage 3 must be blocked on it, and its pass/fail thresholds must use a yardstick measured in the same harness, because prepare-time event timings overstate throughput by 20-25%.
justification: The question is the right one, but the fixed thresholds are miscalibrated. Stage 2 streamed compressed weights at 1.4-1.6 TB/s with the MMA attached (pooler 40.3 vs 19.0 us incumbent). The tie point is real: master's pooler m=1 swap-AB kernel takes 18.6 us in the profile for 67.1 MB, which is 3.6 TB/s raw. At ratio 0.761 (51.1 MB compressed) the decoder must deliver about 2.7 TB/s compressed just to tie, before any MMA or x work. That is borderline, not hopeless, on paper: 3.6 TB/s raw is about 1.8e12 bf16/s, or about 7 elements per SM-cycle over 132 SMs, which leaves a budget of roughly 15-18 lane-instructions per element for exp4 decode. So a measurement is needed. WEAKEST LINK: the DECISION compares absolute prepare-measured TB/s to 2.7/3.3, but LESSONS 2026-10-25 (harvest) says prepare CUDA-event timings undercount the judge profile by 20-25%. A prepare reading of 3.0 TB/s is therefore about 2.4-2.5 TB/s in profile terms, which is a kill, while the rule as written would call it a tie. FIX: in the same prepare harness, with the same cold-L2 flush and event method, also time master's own pooler m=1 _bf16_swapab_kernel path (or _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl at m=1) as the YARDSTICK. Decide on ratios: decode-only cold time / yardstick time <= ~0.85 means revive (it leaves room for MMA+x), 0.85-1.0 means dead for mma.sync, > 1.0 means DEAD. Keep the copy-only variant: if copy-only itself is slower than the yardstick, the ring, not the decoder, is the limiter, and that is also a kill for this design. The warm/L2-resident qkv number is diagnostic only: every timed replay starts with a cold L2 (TASK.md), so it must not enter the decision.
confounders: None. kernel_fn is byte-identical to master and no landed path is touched. Any headline or row movement is run-to-run noise, and the harvest must say so (expected flat everywhere).
interference: No companion. The readout is the [decode-probe] lines, not the rows. The yardstick timing inside the same run replaces any control. Without the yardstick, one run would be ambiguous because of the 20-25% prepare undercount. With it, the run is decisive.
rules_flags: Not a rules or spirit-clause concern. prepare() is explicitly untimed. The probe's timing is print-only and selects nothing, kernel_fn is master's, and nothing derived from `data` is cached. The 'work outside the timed call' concern applies to moving per-call work out of kernel_fn, and this moves nothing.

Leave no residue: free the compressed buffers, the 256 MB flush buffer and the dummy output before prepare() returns (del + torch.cuda.empty_cache() is optional), so the state and memory footprint match master's. If any compressed tensor stays in state, it is just extra memory, but there is no reason to keep it.
Budget: TASK.md gives prepare() up to 300 s, not 10 minutes. The stage-2 build (~52 s) plus the encoder plus about 1 s of launches fits, but print cumulative seconds.

Fault safety (LESSONS 2026-10-25): an illegal-instruction fault in a prepare() kernel poisons the CUDA context, and try/except cannot save the run. The stage-2 decoder already ran on the judge, so the risk is low, but build with -lineinfo, keep TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a, sync and print after each config, and run it as an okc check only (it is one). The rules forbid starting a child process, so do not try one.
No cuobjdump or other process-spawning diagnostics. Use cudaFuncGetAttributes for regs/spills.
open_questions: Before dispatch, set bf16-lossless-exp4-warpspec-persistent-stage3 to depends_on this probe (or hold it), so the line cannot spend a stage-3 check before the probe decides. If the user prefers to spend nothing more on the line, close both now. LESSONS already supports that.

At harvest, record in FINDINGS and LESSONS the decode-only/yardstick ratio, the copy-only/yardstick ratio, and the regs/spills of the best config. On a kill, move the lossless line to Do-not-retry with that number.
